text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Both opposition and government claim successes in negotiations over next year's tax law.
- Heavy machinery group Sket applies for liquidation proceedings in bid to save the company.
- Opposition Social Democrats (SPD) plan to concentrate on growth and employment in their economic policies.
- President Roman Herzog appeals to both trade unions and employers to do more to help the unemployed.
- German industry expresses delight at plans to abolish wealth tax from the beginning of next year.
HANDELSBLATT
- SPD emphasises desire to win in 1998 elections.
- Deutsche Bank denies it plans to cut back its branches as part of a restructuring programme.
- Mannesmann interested in buying ATN Atlas Elektronik unit of beleaguered shipbuilding group Bremer Vulkan.
- Herzog tells trade unionists not to expect too much from the state's social security system.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Sket hopes for help from Chancellor Helmut Kohl.
- Negotiations over next year's tax law present danger of income shortfalls for the government and regional states.
- Roland Issen re-elected as leader of DAG white-collar trade union.
- Germany and Romania agree to work together to combat crime.
DIE WELT
- Economics council of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats propose delaying payment of unemployment benefit for three days after someone registers as jobless.
- Around 70 percent of retailers plan to take advantage of longer shop opening hours from November 1, a survey says.
- DAX share index reaches record high.
